segments.narration: Henry Ford built an American town in the Amazon rainforest. Nineteen twenty-eight, on the Tapajos River in Brazil. He called it Fordlandia.
About two and a half million acres, all for rubber. Clapboard houses, a water tower, hamburgers, square dances, and no alcohol.
Workers rioted in nineteen thirty over the canteen food. But the thing that actually killed Fordlandia was not the people.
Rubber trees grow wild and scattered in the Amazon for a reason. Planted in tight rows, they hand South American leaf blight one continuous meal.
The blight took it. Belterra, downstream, died the same way. In nineteen forty-five Ford's grandson sold both back to Brazil at a loss above twenty million dollars, and Henry Ford never once visited.

verdicts.claim: Henry Ford founded Fordlandia in 1928 on the Tapajos River in Para, Brazil.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia gives 1928, the east bank of the Tapajos about 300 km south of Santarem, Para.

verdicts.claim: The concession covered roughly 2.5 million acres and the site was built as a prefabricated American-style town supporting rubber production.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia: approximately 2.5 million acres (about 10,000 sq km), a prefabricated industrial town intended for 10,000 residents, with American housing and imposed social rules including prohibition.

verdicts.claim: In 1930 Fordlandia workers revolted in the 'Breaking Pans' riot over imposed food and canteen arrangements.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia records the 1930 Quebra-Panelas ('Breaking Pans') revolt over imposed dietary restrictions and food distribution changes.

verdicts.claim: Densely planted rubber trees in the Amazon are devastated by South American leaf blight, which does not spread the same way through scattered wild trees.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia attributes the failure to blight plus ants, lace bugs, red spiders and caterpillars in dense plantations; the contrast with naturally scattered Hevea and with blight-free Asian plantations is the standard account and is given in the Damn Interesting piece.

verdicts.claim: Fordlandia was abandoned in 1934 and its Belterra replacement also failed; in 1945 Henry Ford II sold both back to Brazil at a loss of over $20 million, and Henry Ford never visited.
verdicts.note: Wikipedia: abandoned 1934, operations moved to Belterra, and in 1945 Henry Ford II sold both sites back to Brazil for a loss exceeding $20 million; Ford's never having visited is recorded in both sources.

candidates.text: Henry Ford built an American town in the Amazon rainforest.
candidates.why: A famous name doing something absurd, stated as plain fact.

candidates.text: Ford bought Amazon land the size of a small country.
candidates.why: Scale is strong, but it does not say what he did with it.

candidates.text: A fungus beat Henry Ford out of the Amazon.
candidates.why: Gives away the resolution in the first line.

choice.reason: It is the flattest, most concrete statement of the absurdity and it leaves the entire question of what happened to the town open.
